chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, and Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the girl who has not yet attained puberty: when is it befitting for her to cover her head from those with whom there is no close kinship (mahram), and when is it obligatory upon her to cover her head for the prayer? He (peace be upon him) said: 'She does not cover her head until the prayer becomes obligatory upon her.'
ai.seo_question: When does a girl become obligated to wear a headscarf according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a direct correlation between the onset of religious accountability (*taklif*) and the obligation of hijab, specifying that head covering is not mandatory until the girl reaches the age of prayer. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that specific dress code obligations are tied to the broader framework of *taklif*, distinguishing between general modesty and the legal requirement of covering the head. The hadith serves as a foundational text for determining the precise moment a female child transitions into full religious maturity regarding her public appearance.
